2015_085_102015mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of October 20, 2015 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, carrying recognitions, three sets of September minutes, the August 2015 Treasurer's Report and check register, and reports on evaluation, professional development, post-secondary attainment, the 2014/2015 audit and the 2013 bond program. Total check disbursements for the period were $7,473,038.07 and total disbursements in period $10,322,100.23. The largest single action item is a $69,736.00 Trane U.S. Inc. proposal to restore rather than replace the Athens High School chiller, a decision the administration reports as a savings of over $650,000.00.

Meeting
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, October 20, 2015, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW), Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

Recognition (Item 2)
Sixty-eight (68) students named 2015-16 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, honored at a reception on October 14; semifinalist status reflects scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT. The TSD Mission Moment featured Nithyashree Ramadurai, 17, a Troy High senior and president of the school's Build On chapter who traveled to Haiti to build schools.

Consent Agenda (Item 5)
Minutes of the September 1, 2015 workshop, the September 15, 2015 special meeting and closed session (Resolution 15-087, attorney-client privilege under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c)), the September 15, 2015 regular meeting (Resolutions 15-088 through 15-091, each Yes 7 / No 0), and the Treasurer's Report for August 2015.

Curriculum (Item 7)
Sex Education Advisory Board membership for 2015-2016 (co-chairs Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins) submitted for approval; professional development report for 2015/2016 from Mark Dziatczak; and a post-secondary attainment report covering AP, IB and dual enrollment. In 2014-15 the district recorded 2,902 AP exams from 1,193 testers with 2,392 scores above 3 (82.43%), and 302 full IB Diploma candidates at the International Academy with 96.7% earning the diploma.

Business (Item 8)
David R. Youngstrom, CPA of Yeo & Yeo, P.C. presented the 2014/2015 audit, showing General Fund revenues and other sources of $136,589,446 and expenditures and other uses of $137,267,824 for the year ended June 30, 2015, a material weakness in payroll rate changes, and an unfunded pension liability of over $177mm. The Board is asked to accept the statements, with final reports to issue once the Michigan Auditor General completes its audit of the GASB 68 numbers. A Trane U.S. Inc. proposal of $69,736.00 for the Athens chiller restoration is recommended as a Capital Projects Fund expenditure.

Other (Item 10)
2015/2016 Board committee assignments (revised September 1, 2015); a Barton Malow bond projects update dated 9.9.15; and the Superintendent's 2015-2016 goals, which include successful passage of the November millage renewal and a Facility Review Committee report to the Board in February 2016.

RECOGNITION. The Board adopted a resolution honoring sixty-eight (68) 2015-2016 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, with copies presented at an October 14 reception; the packet notes more than one million students from some 22,000 high schools entered and only 16,000 seniors were named semifinalists, a distinction requiring a score in the top one and one-half percent (1.5%) on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test with comparable SAT scores. Named semifinalists include Swapnil Akunuri, Sujai Arakali, Ajay Balaji, Benjamin Balas, Sirisha Billa, Anurag Bolneni, Sathvik Byreddy, Alex Chen, Angela Chen, Christopher Chen, Satya Chitturi, Jiwoo Choe, Jennifer Cui, Deepthi Devireddy, Kevin Fietsam, Jerry Gao, Michelle Gu, Natalia Jenuwine, Kathryn Jorgensen, Hareena Kaur, Noshin Khan, Michael Kolakowski, Aditi Krishnan, Lena Leszinsky, Eva Lisowski, Claudia Macri, Erin Mitchell, Rohit Nair, Leena Penumalee, Arjun Puri, Huda Rabbani, Nithyashree Ramadurai, Emily Schram, Neil Shah, Sukhnayak Sohi, Thejas Suvarna, Ciara Timban, Apurva Virkud, David Wu, Julia Xu, Demi Yang, Eric Yu, Andrew Yuan, Alex Zhang and Addison Zhou. The TSD Mission Moment featured Nithya (Nithyashree) Ramadurai, age 17, a Troy High senior and president of the school's Build On chapter, a state representative for the organization who volunteers monthly in Metro Detroit and traveled to Haiti to build schools, where the packet states there are only enough schools to serve a quarter of the school-age population; she plans a career with Doctors Without Borders and was introduced by Troy High counselor Jesse Allgeier.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item 5): A, minutes of the September 1, 2015 Board workshop; B, minutes of the September 15, 2015 special meeting and closed session; C, minutes of the September 15, 2015 regular meeting; D, Treasurer's Report for August 2015. The September 1 workshop, at the Administration Building, was called to order by President Philippart at 6:00 p.m. with Dr. Philippart, Mrs. Edmunds, Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Hauff, Mr. Miletti, Mr. Schmidt and Ms. Underwood present, plus Superintendent Machesky and administrators West, Carson, Dziatczak, Griffor and Harris and about five audience members; the agenda covered a bond update, monthly financial report, food service, technology (department personnel, teaching/learning focus, Schoology, early childhood), a teaching and learning update and a millage renewal item, adjourning at 8:50 p.m. (submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary). The September 15 special meeting convened at 6:32 p.m.; Resolution 15-087, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Schmidt, took the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) to discuss an attorney-client privilege, with roll call Yes from Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming and Hauff; closed session ran 6:30 to 6:58 p.m. and the meeting adjourned at 7:01 p.m. The September 15 regular meeting ran 7:03 to 9:09 p.m. with approximately 50 audience members and included Resolution 15-088 approving consent items A through G (including Second Reading and Adoption of Board Policy J-3306, Epinephrine Auto-Injectors, and the July 2015 Treasurer's Report), Resolution 15-089 approving 28 new hires, Resolution 15-090 approving up to $4,000 for professional services pertaining to the evaluation of vacant property as a Capital Maintenance Fund expenditure, and Resolution 15-091 amending the 2015 Tax Rate Request Form L-4029 for a rounding error that should have been carried to the 1,000th decimal place - each vote Yes 7 / No 0. Recognitions in those minutes include MASB Honor Board and Standard of Excellence awards, a Master Diamond Award to Dr. Nancy Philippart, a Master Platinum Award to Gary Hauff, service recognition for Paula Fleming (12 years), Gary Hauff (14 years) and Ida Edmunds (30 years); the ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the CAFR for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2014, crediting Rick West; and the 2015 Outstanding Superintendent Communicator Award to Dr. Rich Machesky from the Michigan School Public Relations Association, presented by MSPRA Board Member Rebecca Fannon and citing OneTROY. Enrollment as of September 8, 2015 came in higher than expected, with elementary up by 70 students, 40 more middle school students (Smith with the most growth), high school numbers down and overall 100 more students than the prior year.

PERSONNEL (Item 6). Probationary 2015-2016 contracts recommended for Sara Cavataio, 1.0 ELD Teacher at Bemis Elementary (M.A.T. and B.S., Oakland University; Professional Teaching Certificate June 2014; Literacy Coach at Holbrook Elementary, Hamtramck, August 2012 to August 2015; Reading Specialist at Kosciuszko Middle School, April 2010 to August 2012; resident of Royal Oak) and Andrea Polite, .7 Resource Room Teacher at Troy Union Elementary (B.S., Wayne State University; Provisional Teaching Certificate May 2014; Resource Room long-term substitute, Romeo Community Schools, October 2014 to June 2015; resident of Sterling Heights). Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, presented the 2014/15 Evaluation Summary, reviewed at the October 6, 2015 workshop: the fourth year of the Troy Educator Appraisal Model (TEAM) with Teachscape, showing 672 Highly Effective, 106 Effective, 5 Minimally Effective and 1 Ineffective teacher ratings in 2014/15, against 573/184/9/2 in 2013/14 and 305/447/4/4 in 2012/13. Administrator evaluation, in its second year using Reeves' Leadership Performance Matrix, showed 26 Highly Effective, 6 Effective and 1 Minimally Effective in 2014-15 and 26/10/1 in 2013-14.

CURRICULUM (Item 7). The Sex Education Advisory Board roster for 2015-2016 (updated 9/15/15) is co-chaired by Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins and includes district personnel Amy Buchanan (Smith Middle School), Lisa Danhoff (Troy High), Karyn Schachinger (Athens High) and Kevin Wilson (Boulan Park Middle School); clergy Rev. David Huseltine of Big Beaver United Methodist Church, 3753 John R Rd.; health resource David Roth of the Oakland Health Department, 1200 N. Telegraph Rd., Pontiac; six parents; resident Diane Trombley; and student Maria Manolias. Mark Dziatczak presented 2015-16 professional development, including an administrative retreat on the Disciplines of Execution and General Stanley McChrystal's Team of Teams, quarterly peer district meetings (October 6 in Rochester, with Ann Arbor, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, East Grand Rapids, Forest Hills, Grosse Pointe, Novi, Okemos, Rochester, Saline and Troy) and four district initiatives: ambitious outcomes for all students, a sustainable teaching and learning leadership network, Cultures of Thinking in all schools and technology integration through Schoology. The Post Secondary Credit Attainment Report shows AP Scholar counts of 85 at Athens (3.10 average) and 117 at Troy High (3.48), TSD total 202 / 3.29; AP Scholar with Honor 48 / 64 / 112; AP Scholar with Distinction 87 / 176 / 263; National AP Scholar 24 / 73 / 97. AP testing in 2014-15 totaled 2,902 exams and 1,193 testers with 2,392 scores above 3 (82.43%), up from 1,888 exams in 08-09. AP Equity and Excellence for 2014-15 was 51.9% at Athens, 57.3% at Troy High and 55.1% districtwide. At the International Academy, 2014-15 average score per test was 5.1 and average total score 31.9; 302 full diploma candidates across three campuses with 96.7% earning the IB Diploma; 952 higher-level exams with 912 above 3 (95.8%); the diploma requires a combined score of 24 across six assessments graded 1 to 7. Niles Community High School dual enrollment requires 21.5 high school credits and shows 24 students plus 6 full-year for Winter 2016 and 6 inaugural full-year students for Fall 2015.

BUSINESS (Item 8). David R. Youngstrom, CPA, audit partner at Yeo & Yeo, P.C., presented the 2014-2015 audit, previously given in draft at the October 6, 2015 workshop; General Fund revenues and other sources were $136,589,446 and expenditures and other uses $137,267,824 for the year ended June 30, 2015. The governance letter reports a material weakness in payroll rate changes and significant deficiencies in unearned revenue and payroll accrual, with management comments on fund balance policy, contract and wage approval, timely bank deposits, outstanding checks, personnel activity reports and Title I matters; single audit findings cover the Nutrition Cluster, Special Education Cluster, Title I and TANF. Future challenges listed include an unfunded pension liability of over $177mm and GASB #75. Item 8.B recommends accepting the statements, with final reports to issue once the Michigan Auditor General completes its audit of the GASB 68 numbers. Item 8.C recommends accepting a Trane U.S. Inc. price proposal of $69,736.00 as a Capital Projects Fund expenditure for the Athens chiller restoration; the October 2, 2015 memorandum from Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, 1140 Rankin, Troy MI 48083, to Rick West states the bond scope had identified replacement but restoration provides an additional 12-15 years of service life and results in a savings of over $650,000.00, priced through The Cooperative Purchasing Network. Trane proposal ID 607980, TCPN quote 34-207843-15-002, covers one Trane CVHF055 chiller, serial L98J05846, at Troy Athens High School, 4333 John R Road; the price includes a Trane Earthwise Purge and a Trane Refrigerant Monitor and a two-year compressor motor warranty contingent on a maintained Trane Service Agreement, with all other content warranted one year parts and 90 days labor; insurance limits are $2,000,000 commercial general liability per occurrence and $2,000,000 automobile liability.

OTHER (Item 10). Board Committee Membership for 2015/2016, revised September 1, 2015, assigns Schmidt to the NCA District Team and Troy Nature Society, Miletti and Edmunds to the Crisis Committee, Underwood to the Diversity Council, Miletti to the District Technology Committee, Edmunds/Hauff/Philippart to Policy, Fleming/Schmidt/Philippart to Superintendent Evaluation, Fleming to Friends of Troy Seniors and Troy Community Coalition, Miletti and Fleming to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, and Edmunds, Hauff, Schmidt and Philippart to the Troy Historical Society. The Barton Malow | TMP 2013 Bond Program Series 1 construction update of 9.9.15 reports BP#5 Troy High additions with Area J completing November 2015, Area F October 2015 and Area G complete; BP#6 Boulan Park and Larson office additions completing end of October; BP#9 Boulan Park and Larson MEP upgrades with boilers, chillers and fire alarm complete and energy management controls in commissioning; and BP#8 Athens High School mechanical and electrical upgrades out for bids in October 2015. Dr. Machesky's 2015-2016 Superintendent goals cover operational visibility measured by a Central Office scorecard, a world class Business Services Department and a transparent 16/17 FY budget process, communications goals including successful passage of the November millage renewal and a Facility Review Committee report and recommendations to the Board in February 2016, a comprehensive all-employee audit of payroll and fringe benefit accounts in the Sungard eFinance database, and teaching and learning goals creating Content Area Teams in K-2 writing, K-12 math, 6-12 ELA, science and social studies with Cultures of Thinking reported in every Continuous Improvement Plan.
